components.name: GlassPillDictationTyping

font.reason: Vazirmatn is a neutral variable UI sans with reliable Persian glyph coverage, matching the original restrained system-input treatment without synthetic bold.

text.timing: The original 0.06–0.73 typing window, cursor cues, and 50-frame duration remain unchanged. The Persian string has 20 code points rather than 18, so its per-character rate is proportionally faster while the same start and end beats are retained.

rtlDecisions.what: Input text, caret and voice-control order
rtlDecisions.why: They communicate text-entry reading order: text starts at the right, the caret follows the Persian prefix toward the left, and the voice action moves to the left end.
The gradient is part of the input’s directional affordance, so its bright control-end is retained after the control mirrors.

rtlDecisions.what: Pill scale/opacity, vertical waveform geometry and sinusoidal breathing
rtlDecisions.why: These are physical or non-reading-direction motion; preserving them maintains the original quiet entrance and resting beat.

typography.shaping: No per-glyph boxes or transforms. typeOn() exposes logical string prefixes so joining is recomputed correctly at every typing step.
typography.measurement: The fixed pill width is measured with offsetWidth from a hidden Vazirmatn run after document.fonts.load(), avoiding fallback-font or stage-transform measurements.

components.rasterHandling: No raster or external visual assets are used.

visualVerification.observations: Compared corresponding original and Persian stills for pop-in, cursor-first state, early/mid/late typing, glow fade and final neutral pill. Persian frames are clean and contain no foreign visible text.

lessons: When a measurement node sits inside a scaled DesignStage, use offsetWidth rather than getBoundingClientRect().width; the latter includes stage scaling and can make a fixed Persian input pill dramatically oversized.
